title: Daisy motif — basic
subtitle: Eight double-crochet petals around a tight chain-ring centre, 9 cm
excerpt: Eight simple petals worked on chain loops from a centre ring give this 9 cm daisy its clean, flat shape. The petals are rows of double crochet worked back and forth on individual chain foundations, so the motif needs no specialist stitches and lies flat without blocking. It joins into wreaths, garlands, and grid throws.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 2 (1886), flower motif section (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), crochet daisy chapter.

glossaryTerms.definition: A loop formed by joining a length of chain with a slip stitch. Used as the flower centre when a visible ring is acceptable, as opposed to the invisible magic ring.

content.text: The basic daisy works eight flat petals outward from a
chain ring

centre. Each petal is a separate back-and-forth rectangle of double crochet on a 10-chain foundation, attached at the base to the ring. No specialist stitches are needed — this is double crochet and chain only, and it lies flat without blocking. Two colours (centre ring in a contrast colour, petals in white or cream) give the clearest daisy read.

The petals can be worked all in one go around the ring, attaching each to the next with a single slip stitch at the centre ring before beginning the chain foundation of the next petal. Keep the chain foundation even — pulling the chain tighter on the first petal and looser on the eighth produces petals of different widths, which throws the symmetry.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 5 g of DK-weight cotton in white or cream, plus a small amount of a contrast colour for the centre ring. A 4 mm crochet hook. Tapestry needle. Scissors.

content.text: Gauge
Each finished basic daisy measures 9 cm across in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook. No blocking required; the petals lie flat naturally.
Stitches used
chain (ch) — UK and US shared.
slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc) — UK; US "single crochet".
Pattern
Centre ring

In contrast colour: Ch 6. Sl st to first ch to form a ring. Ch 1 (does not count as a stitch). Work 12dc into the ring. Sl st to first dc to join. Do not fasten off; drop contrast colour and join petal colour.
Petals
Work 8 petals as follows, spacing them evenly around the centre ring by anchoring each at the next dc of the ring:

Ch 10. Turn. Sk first ch, dc across next 8 ch. (8 dc.) Turn. Ch 1 (does not count as stitch). Dc across all 8 sts. (8 dc.) Turn. Ch 1. Dc across all 8 sts. (8 dc.) Sl st back to the next dc of the centre ring to anchor this petal and start the next.

Repeat this petal sequence 7 more times, anchoring each to the next dc of the centre ring. After the 8th petal, sl st to the dc of the ring adjacent to where you started. Fasten off. (8 petals total, each 8 dc wide and 3 rows deep.)

definition.title: Daisy motif — basic
definition.caption: Centre ring with eight petal foundations. Each petal is three rows of 8dc worked back and forth on a 10-chain foundation, anchored to the ring at base.

content.text: Finishing

Fasten off petal colour. Pick up the dropped contrast colour and weave it in through the back of the ring stitches. Trim all tails to 1 cm. The motif lies flat without pinning; a light steam-press (not a steam iron directly on the petals) can neaten any uneven edges.
Joining

For a garland, join daisies through a corner stitch of adjacent petals with a length of chain. For a flat throw, whipstitch through the outermost row of each petal edge to neighbour. The layered daisy (crochet-daisy-layered-petals) adds a second ring of petals between the first eight.
Care
Handwash in cool water with mild soap, or machine-wash on a wool cycle. Lay flat on a clean towel and ease to shape while damp.
What to try next

The layered daisy (crochet-daisy-layered-petals) adds a second ring of petals in a shorter length, creating a double-layer flower with more depth. The bobble-centre daisy (crochet-daisy-bobble-centre) replaces the flat chain ring with a cluster of bobble stitches for a raised three-dimensional centre.
